newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, more W.African booked for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, more W.African booked for Asia.

text.p: Asian crudes were steady on Thursday, but trading of heavy sweet crude was limited while sellers stood back to wait for the Indonesia export allocations early next week.
Instead, activity was dominated by West African trades to Asian refiners, with more than 10 million barrels already sold this week all for July lifting, traders said.
A VLCC of Cabinda/Nemba and Odudu loading around 10 July was heard sold to a South Korean refiner.
This was in addition to two VLCCs, of Djeno/Palanca and Qua Iboe/Zafiru traded to South Korea earlier.
Possibly four 900,000-barrel cargoes of Cabinda were also heard done to China, traders said.
Details of China trades were unclear, but the average price of the cargoes was heard to be dated Brent -1.00 per barrel.

Taiwan emerged to take advantage of the narrow Brent/Dubai differential, buying two million barrels of second half July loading Forcados/N'Kossa crudes on the spot market, on top of its monthly term supplies of West African grades.
In contrast, thin demand kept light Asian crudes under pressure, with a July cargo of Kutubu offered by a major at APPI Tapis -70.

A very prompt June cargo of Kutubu was widely heard done at more than 1.00 under APPI Tapis, but traders did not see the level as a true reflection of the market since the cargo was distressed. It was heard loading as early as this week.
July Belida was sold to a U.S. major at ICP +40, but Belida prices were expected to weaken, due to the maintenance shutdown of Indonesia's Balikpapan refinery in July.
Balikpapan refines a large volume of Belida, traders said.
The Mideast crude market was lacklustre, apart from rumours that the last Umm Shaif cargo was done at ADNOC -27.
